$x=\frac{t}{2},\,y={e}^{t}$
from $t=0$ to $t=1$ (shown above)?
after.worked_solution:
To compute the arc length $L$ of a parametrically defined curve, we use the formula

$$
L={\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t.
$$

Computing the derivatives of $x$ and $y,$ we have
We have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{t}{2})=\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t})={e}^{t}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute these derivatives in the formula for arc length, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\sqrt{{(\frac{1}{2})}^{2}+{({e}^{t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\sqrt{({e}^{2t})+(\frac{1}{4})}\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}\sqrt{4{e}^{2t}+1}\,\text{d}t\,.\end{aligned}

Which of the following gives the length of the curve defined by the parametric equations
$x=\frac{t}{2},\,y={e}^{t}$
from $t=0$ to $t=1$ (shown above)?
content.worked_solution:
To compute the arc length $L$ of a parametrically defined curve, we use the formula

$$
L={\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t.
$$

Computing the derivatives of $x$ and $y,$ we have
We have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{t}{2})=\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t})={e}^{t}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute these derivatives in the formula for arc length, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\sqrt{{(\frac{1}{2})}^{2}+{({e}^{t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\sqrt{({e}^{2t})+(\frac{1}{4})}\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}\sqrt{4{e}^{2t}+1}\,\text{d}t\,.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: The arc length is ∫₀²√((dx/dt)²+(dy/dt)²) dt. Here dx/dt=eᵗ and dy/dt=1, so the length is ∫₀²√(e²ᵗ+1) dt, matching option b.

Which of the following gives the length of the curve defined by the parametric equations
$x={e}^{t},\,y=t$
from $t=0$ to $t=2$ (shown above)?
after.worked_solution:
To compute the arc length $L$ of a parametrically defined curve, we use the formula

$$
L={\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t.
$$

Computing the derivatives of $x$ and $y,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t})={e}^{t}\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)=1.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute these derivatives in the formula for arc length, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\sqrt{({e}^{t})^{2}+(1)^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\sqrt{{e}^{2t}+1}\,\text{d}t\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following gives the length of the curve defined by the parametric equations
$x={e}^{t},\,y=t$
from $t=0$ to $t=2$ (shown above)?
content.worked_solution:
To compute the arc length $L$ of a parametrically defined curve, we use the formula

$$
L={\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t.
$$

Computing the derivatives of $x$ and $y,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t})={e}^{t}\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)=1.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute these derivatives in the formula for arc length, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\sqrt{({e}^{t})^{2}+(1)^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\sqrt{{e}^{2t}+1}\,\text{d}t\,.\end{aligned}
$$
